## TL;DR

Completed the mobile design audit and corrected the Search overlay input’s mobile touch height from 36px to 44px. The audit now covers the requested page families, login and full-screen diff routes, checks text contrast in both themes where the rendered surfaces were available, and records concrete follow-up fixes with RepoOS attachment evidence. The remaining work is assigned to focused tasks #1147–#1151 or the existing #1145 task.

## Work and rationale

The task called for a rendered product review rather than a source-only pass. I used a 390 × 844 CSS-pixel phone viewport with touch emulation and reviewed the auth-less worktree app across Mission Control, Work queue and task detail, Search and More, Settings, Stories, Releases, Agents, Checks, Inputs, Context, Deployments, Secrets, Dev, Client board, login and the full-screen task/repository diff routes. I sampled long task and story names, release warnings, empty Checks and diff states, and both light and dark themes for the principal page families.

The report is now stored at `docs/audits/mobile-design-audit-1146.md`, matching the repository’s audit-document convention. It records route, viewport, severity, impact, evidence and a concrete fix for each substantial finding. The evidence links point to RepoOS attachments, which remain available to reviewers and readers of the branch. The report notes that the full-screen diff captures were light-only, that the diff views rendered empty states, and that signed-in-only Secrets/Agents data was unavailable in the auth-less preview. It does not present those as verified states.

The visible small fix is in the shared Search overlay: the phone input now has a 44px minimum height, matching the project’s mobile touch-target convention. The close control already measures 44 × 44px. I kept the change scoped to the mobile rule so desktop sizing is preserved.

The audit found that the shared DiffView Back control measures 76 × 28px, below the 44px height floor; this is assigned to #1151. The task-detail tab strip and preview helper have their own scoped follow-up in #1147. That task explicitly excludes the title/header and Mission Control alignment handled by #1145. Other findings are assigned to #1148 (Settings navigation density), #1149 (Checks intro/actions), and #1150 (Stories identity truncation). The More backdrop and idle pipeline overlay remain with #1145. This avoids duplicating the active shared-chrome work.

The report also evaluates sampled text/background contrast in both themes and records the boundary of that check: text pairs sampled were at least 4.5:1, while icons and status tints were not exhaustively certified. The More backdrop remains visually weak and is tracked by #1145.

## Approaches tried

I first reviewed the existing audit and its first review report, then compared the stated method against the repository’s 44px touch convention and the active follow-up task scopes. I checked the task board state and task attachment list through RepoOS, verified that #1147’s current scope is limited to tabs/helper copy, and reviewed the audit image inventory in the worktree. I retained RepoOS attachment URLs in the report rather than relying on local `.repoos/audit-1146` captures, which are ignored by Git.

For the visual sweep, I used rendered states instead of inferring layout from Vue/CSS source. I checked routes in the router and included the separate full-screen diff surfaces, because these do not appear inside the task drawer. I used measured rendered bounds for the Search and DiffView Back controls and separate the checked 44px floor from the below-floor shared Back control.

## Challenges and blockers

The mandated `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed: format, lint, build, contrast, scoped tests and UI smoke all passed. The auth-less preview cannot provide real signed-in Secrets content or all signed-in Agents states, so those states remain unverified. The captured diff routes showed “No diff available”; this allowed review of route framing and Back-control geometry, but not long diff content density. The audit viewport was 390px wide, so a separate 320px stress pass remains useful. These boundaries are stated in the report rather than treated as successful coverage.

The task CLI warns that board reads from a linked worktree use the control-plane checkout. I used RepoOS for the task metadata/attachment state and kept source/report edits within this worktree. No changes were made to task frontmatter by hand.

## Key learnings

A shared mobile touch-target floor needs to be applied to measured rendered bounds, not inferred from a control’s visual style or width alone. Page-level overflow checks would miss the 28px DiffView Back control. Mobile layout issues also cluster by hierarchy: headers, tab strips, intro/action groups and navigation layers need their own phone compositions even when the global shell behaves consistently.

Rendered evidence should live in RepoOS attachments when it supports a durable audit. Local ignored screenshots are useful during inspection but make poor report references. Finally, audit findings are most actionable when each one names its route, impact, severity, proposed fix and owning task, while clearly crediting adjacent work already assigned elsewhere.
